transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good evening, thank you for calling S-Net broadband technical support. My name is Daniel speaking today. How can I help you this evening?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Daniel, it's Priyanka calling. I'm ringing because my fibre broadband keeps dropping out every single evening and it's driving me up the wall.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand how frustrating it is when your connection drops right in the middle of your evening, Priyanka, and I'll get straight onto sorting this out for you.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, I appreciate that. It literally happens like clockwork between half seven and ten o'clock at night while I'm trying to stream or finish work calls.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So if I've got that right, your daytime service is stable, but every night between roughly seven thirty and ten your fibre connection keeps cutting out completely—is that accurate?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, spot on. During the day while I'm working from home on spreadsheets it's mostly fine, maybe a tiny dip, but in the evening it completely dies.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Got it, thank you for confirming that. Before I pull up your live line telemetry, could you confirm the first line of your address and your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, the first line is 14 Meadowcroft Lane, Guildford, and my four-digit PIN is 7392.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Lovely, thank you Priyanka, I've verified your account now. I can see you're on our Full Fibre 300 package. Which router setup are you running at home right now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've got the black S-Net Hub 4X sitting on the hallway table next to the main Openreach optical box on the wall.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, and when the connection drops in the evening, what happens to the status light on the front of your router? Does it flash amber, turn red, or stay white?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Actually, now that you ask, the main light on the front stays solid white most of the time, or occasionally flashes green for twenty seconds, while my laptop says no internet.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a very useful clue, Priyanka. And on the white Openreach optical box on the wall—the ONT—do the PON and LOS lights change colour when this happens?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, I checked the little wall box last night when the television froze. The PON light stayed solid green and the LOS light was completely off.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, that tells me the physical fibre optic laser coming from the street cabinet into your hallway is staying locked, or at least not losing optical sync entirely.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, so if the fibre line coming into the house is green, why are my laptop, my partner's tablet, and the living room smart TV all losing connection at once?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's dig into both possibilities. First, are any of your devices plugged directly into the yellow gigabit Ethernet ports on the back with a cable, or is everything on Wi-Fi?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Everything is on Wi-Fi because the hallway socket is in an awkward spot and we didn't want trailing cables across the floorboards into the lounge.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That makes complete sense. And when your devices drop out at eight o'clock, do they lose the Wi-Fi signal icon altogether, or do they stay connected with an exclamation mark?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sometimes the Wi-Fi network disappears from the list for about forty seconds and then pops back up, and other times it stays connected but pages just spin forever.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If the Wi-Fi network name actually vanishes for forty seconds and comes back, that usually means either the wireless radio is crashing or the router itself is doing a soft reboot.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: A soft reboot? Why would it be rebooting itself every evening without anyone touching it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me inspect your router's internal event log from my console right now to see what happened over the last seventy-two hours. Give me just a second to load the diagnostic tree.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Take your time, I just want to get to the bottom of it so tomorrow night isn't another repeat.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Aha, looking at your event table from last night at 20:14 and 21:08, and the night before at 19:52, your router logged a kernel radio reset triggered by Smart Channel Switching.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Smart Channel Switching? What does that mean in plain English?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Basically, in the evening when all your neighbours come home and start streaming on their routers, the wireless airwaves around Meadowcroft Lane get heavily congested.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, there are quite a few terraced houses and flats right next to us, you can see about fifteen different Wi-Fi names when you open your phone settings.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly. When Smart Channel Switching detects heavy interference on your current channel, it tries to hop to a cleaner frequency automatically.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, shouldn't that be a good thing though? Why is it knocking us offline?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It should be seamless, Priyanka, but I can see your router is currently running firmware version 4.14.0, which has a known bug when DFS radar channels are scanned during peak evening traffic.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh! So instead of switching channels smoothly, the bug makes the whole wireless chip crash and restart?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Precisely. Whenever it tries to jump onto channel 52 or 100 in the evening, the radio driver hangs, drops all connected devices for forty seconds, and resets the DHCP lease table.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That explains why both my work laptop and the TV drop at the exact same second even though the green light on the wall box stays solid!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Spot on. Now, I also checked the exchange PPP session logs maintained by our core network diagnostics team just to verify whether there were any external line drops.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Do you need to transfer me over to that core network diagnostics team, or can we sort it here?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No transfer needed at all, Priyanka—I have full access to the provisioning tools right here, so I'll log the line monitor myself and handle everything from here from start to finish.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh brilliant, thank you Daniel, I really didn't fancy being passed around three different departments tonight.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You won't be, I promise. Here is what I am going to do for you right now: first, I'll disable the buggy auto-DFS hopping and lock your 5 gigahertz band to channel 44.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, will channel 44 still give us the full three hundred megabits speed in the living room?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, channel 44 is a high-power non-DFS channel, and scanning your router's neighbourhood survey right now, zero neighbouring routers within range are using channel 44.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That sounds promising. And what about the older devices like our smart plugs and the kitchen radio?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Those connect on the 2.4 gigahertz band. Right now yours is stuck on channel 6, which has seven overlapping neighbours, so I'm moving that over to channel 1 at a clean 20 megahertz width.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, and what about that firmware bug you mentioned? Can you update the software on the router so it doesn't crash again?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I am going to push firmware version 4.18.2 directly to your router now, which patches that wireless driver hang permanently.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How long does the firmware update take? Will it cut this phone call off?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Since you're calling me on your mobile over 4G rather than Wi-Fi calling, we won't get disconnected while the router restarts.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I turned Wi-Fi off on my mobile before ringing you just in case the broadband died mid-sentence.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Very smart move. Please bear with me and allow me to place you on a brief hold for about ninety seconds while I push the firmware patch and channel lock to your router.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure thing Daniel, I'll stay on the line.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Priyanka, I really appreciate your patience while that firmware image flashed across.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No problem at all! I was watching the hallway table—the light went pulsing blue for a minute and it's just turned solid white again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Solid white means the boot sequence completed cleanly and the new radio parameters are active. Let me refresh my telemetry screen to verify the software build number.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, my phone and laptop are just reconnecting to the Wi-Fi network now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: While my management screen refreshes the device inventory, which router model have you got sitting there, is it the Hub 3 or the Hub 4?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Er, like I mentioned earlier at the start of the call, it's the black S-Net Hub 4X.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Ah, yes, the Hub 4X, apologies—it's just refreshed on my diagnostic pane now and shows hardware revision 4X running firmware version 4.18.2.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, okay. Does it show the new Wi-Fi channels locked in properly on your screen?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, it does! Your 2.4 gigahertz band is locked on channel 1, and your 5 gigahertz band is locked on channel 44 with Smart Channel Switching disabled.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me open my work laptop right now and see how fast pages are loading.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please do, and if you can open a browser and run a quick speed check on speed.s-net.co.uk, let's see what throughput you're getting in the lounge.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hang on, I'm clicking start test on the laptop now... wow, the needle went straight up to 312 megabits per second download!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: 312 megabits over Wi-Fi in the lounge is right at the top of your Full Fibre 300 profile, Priyanka. What is the upload reading and the latency ping?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Upload is 51 megabits per second, and the ping is 6 milliseconds with zero jitter.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Six milliseconds with zero jitter is rock solid. And how is the living room smart TV behaving now—has it reconnected cleanly?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, my partner just put a 4K stream on in the living room and it started playing instantaneously without any buffering wheel.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fantastic news. I have also enabled a 7-day automated stability monitor on your line from my desk, so if the router logs any unexpected radio resets, I'll get an alert directly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Do I need to do anything if it stays fine over the next week?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Nothing at all. If the line stays completely clean for seven days, the monitor closes automatically and sends you a confirmation text.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And what if by some bad luck it drops out again tomorrow night?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I've put my direct case reference SN-884192 in an SMS to your mobile right now; if anything flickers, reply to that text and it routes straight back to my queue.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've just received the text message with reference SN-884192. That gives me a lot of peace of mind.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm really glad we could get that firmware updated and those congested channels cleared out for you tonight, Priyanka.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, everything is working super fast now and we know exactly why it was crashing every evening.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we wrap up, are you happy that your connection issue is resolved tonight, and is there anything else I can help you with on your account?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that's everything sorted, thank you so much for explaining it all clearly, Daniel.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It has been an absolute pleasure helping you tonight, Priyanka. Thank you for choosing S-Net, and have a wonderful, uninterrupted evening!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Daniel, have a lovely evening too. Bye!
